correctness.rationale: Every idempotent is the identity on a union of full blocks, yielding an intrinsic Boolean semilattice. Preservation of common natural-order upper bounds for rank-one arrow pairs forces the block-atom permutation to be identity or reversal. Composable rank-one arrows form a connected groupoid; their image label maps necessarily are a single group automorphism conjugated by normalized vertex gauges. Rank-one restrictions have joins equal to all higher-rank maps, proving completeness and uniqueness. The converse formula preserves multiplication by cancellation of gauges. The independent exhaustive verifier checked 300340 multiplication equations across three finite configurations. The \(S_6\) exception uses the established symmetric-group outer automorphism theorem.

originality.rationale: The full 2019 defining paper calculates rank and presentations but not abstract automorphisms; the full 2011 partial-endomorphism paper proves spatiality for monoids with point-valued constant idempotents, absent here when block size is greater than one. The concrete \(m=6\) non-spatial class could not be subsumed by the cited spatiality results. A classical theorem on Out(\(S_6\)) is used as input but gives no monoid extension. Published research-record searches and accessible previously studied claims revealed no equal or stronger statement; an unlocated more general labelled-rook theorem remains a genuine risk.

value.rationale: This is a complete, intrinsic, uniform structural classification of the automorphism groups of the natural ordered-uniform-block inverse monoids used as generators of the normally ordered pseudovariety. The theorem determines exact orders and all abstract symmetries and exposes a sharp spatiality boundary at block size six, where precisely half the automorphisms cannot arise by permutations of the underlying points. This exceptional bridge from Out(\(S_6\)) to monoid automorphisms is mathematically motivated by symmetry rigidity rather than by an arbitrary finite computation. The result also supplies a normal form for exploring labelled inverse monoids more generally.
